title: WiFi Scanner Radar
intro: Find the WiFi networks around you and show how strong each one is.

steps.title: Scan the airwaves
steps.text:
`WiFi.scanNetworks()` listens for every WiFi network nearby and gives how many it found. `WiFi.SSID(i)` is a network's name and `WiFi.RSSI(i)` its signal strength in **dBm**: closer to 0 is stronger.

**Your task:** Run, open the **Serial Monitor**, and look at the list. Which network is strongest?
hints: The scan takes a few seconds.
-40 dBm is very strong; -90 dBm is very weak.
Walk around with the board and scan again.
steps.success: Your board can see all the WiFi around it.

steps.title: Signal bars
steps.text:
dBm numbers are hard to read. The `bars()` function turns them into 0 to 4 bars, like a phone does.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks for 3 bars (stronger than -67) and 2 bars (stronger than -75).
hints: The `if`s go from strongest to weakest.
3 bars is stronger than -67, 2 bars is stronger than -75.
steps.success: Easy to read at a glance.

steps.title: The radar screen
steps.text: **Goal:** show the scan on the OLED: how many networks, then up to 6 network names, each with bars that grow taller from left to right. Scan again every 5 seconds.
hints: Each line is 9 pixels tall: `y = 12 + i * 9`.
`fillRect(x, y, width, height, SSD1306_WHITE)` draws a bar.
`.substring(0, 14)` cuts long names short so they fit.

checks.label: My radar shows the networks around me

steps.success: A WiFi radar! Now you can find the best spot for WiFi.

outro: Your radar **scans** the airwaves, measures **signal strength** (RSSI, in dBm) and turns it into bars. Phones show WiFi bars exactly this way.
stretch: Count how many networks are open (no password) and show the number.
Sort the networks from strongest to weakest before showing them.
Make an LED blink faster when your favourite network is stronger.
